title.ja: 桂馬の動き方

explain.ja: 桂馬は、前に2マス進んで横に1マスずれたマスへ動けます。
explain.en: The knight moves two squares forward and one square to the side.

section.ja: 桂馬の動き方、前に2つ横に1つ先のマスに動ける
section.en: How the knight moves: two squares forward and one to the side

title.ja: 成銀の動き方

explain.ja: 桂馬が成ると成桂になり、金将と同じ動きになります。縦横1マスと斜め前に動けるようになり、進める方向が大きく変わります。飛車・角・香車は遠くへ動けても途中の駒を飛び越せませんが、桂馬だけは他の駒を飛び越せます。
explain.en: A promoted knight becomes a promoted knight piece that moves like gold: one square orthogonally or diagonally forward, so its available directions change greatly. Rook, bishop and lance cannot jump over pieces in their way, but the knight alone can.

section.ja: 成桂の動き方、成ると金の動きに
section.en: How the promoted knight moves: promoted, it moves like a gold

title.ja: 桂馬は他の駒を跳び越えられる
title.en: The knight can jump over other pieces

explain.ja: 「攻めは飛角銀桂」という格言のとおり、桂馬は基本的に攻めに使う駒です。桂馬特有のトリッキーな動きで他の駒を狙うのが効果的です。
explain.en: As the proverb "attack with rook, bishop, silver and knight" says, the knight is basically an attacking piece. Use its tricky movement to target other pieces.

section.ja: 桂馬は他の駒を跳び越えられる
section.en: The knight can jump over other pieces

label.ja: 駒を飛び越えてはダメ

title.ja: 図1-1 桂馬を跳ねていいのか？
title.en: Figure 1-1: Should the knight jump forward?

explain.ja: 桂馬の使い方で一番大事なのは、むやみに跳ねないことです。「桂馬の高跳び歩の餌食」という格言があり、どんどん跳ねると歩で取られる展開になりがちです。たとえば図1-1で何も考えず▲3七桂と跳ねる指し方がそれにあたります。
explain.en: The key point in using the knight is not to jump it out carelessly. The proverb "a high-jumping knight is prey for a pawn" warns that hopping the knight forward easily lets it be captured by a pawn. For instance, playing ▲3七桂 in Figure 1-1 without thinking is exactly that.

section.ja: 桂馬の高跳び歩の餌食
section.en: The knight's high jump falls prey to a pawn

title.ja: 図1-2 桂馬を跳ねたところ

explain.ja: 図1-1から▲3七桂と跳ねた局面です。一見自然な活用に見えますが、悪手になります。
explain.en: This is the position after ▲3七桂 from Figure 1-1. It looks like a natural way to use the knight but is a bad move.

section.ja: 桂馬の高跳び歩の餌食
section.en: The knight's high jump falls prey to a pawn

title.ja: 図1-3 桂馬が取られてしまう

explain.ja: 桂馬は前のマスに進めないため、頭に歩を打たれると簡単に取られてしまうことがあります。後手は歩を捨てて桂頭にスペースを作り、歩で攻めるのが好手で、これで桂馬はどうやっても取られてしまいます。
explain.en: A knight cannot move to the square directly ahead, so a pawn placed on its head can easily win it. White's good move was to sacrifice a pawn to open space above the knight's head and attack with a pawn, after which the knight cannot avoid capture.

section.ja: 桂馬の高跳び歩の餌食
section.en: The knight's high jump falls prey to a pawn

title.ja: 図1-4 桂頭を守る手が重要
title.en: Figure 1-4: Protecting the square in front of the knight is important

explain.ja: 桂馬を跳ねる前に、▲4八銀から▲4七銀と銀を繰り出して桂頭の3六をカバーしておくのがよいでしょう。そうすれば桂頭に歩を打たれても銀で取り返せます。コツはむやみに跳ねないことで、狙いがなければ初期位置のまま動かさないのも戦略です。桂馬は成ると動きが大きく変わり、基本的に成桂のほうが強いとされますが、状況によってはあえて成らないのも有効です。
explain.en: Before jumping the knight, bring the silver out with ▲4八銀 and ▲4七銀 to cover the square at 3六, the knight's head. Then if a pawn is dropped there, the silver can recapture. The knack is not to jump needlessly; if there is no aim, leaving the knight at home is a valid strategy. The knight's movement changes a lot on promotion, and a promoted knight is generally stronger, but declining to promote can be right in some situations.

section.ja: 桂馬の高跳び歩の餌食
section.en: The knight's high jump falls prey to a pawn

title.ja: 成る？成らない？

explain.ja: むやみに桂馬を跳ね出すと、歩で取られる展開になりがちです。特に狙いがなければ、初期位置のまま動かさないのも戦略です。また、桂馬は成ると動きが大きく変わる駒です。成桂のほうが強力とされますが、状況によっては、あえて成らないのも良いでしょう。
explain.en: Jumping the knight out carelessly tends to get it captured by a pawn. Without a specific aim, leaving it on its starting square is also a valid strategy. The knight also changes its movement greatly when promoted; a promoted knight is generally stronger, but depending on the situation it can be fine not to promote.

section.ja: 相手の陣地で成らないのもOK
section.en: Not promoting in the opponent's camp is also fine

label.ja: 成る？ 不成？ 選べる

title.ja: 図2-1 ふんどしの桂

explain.ja: ここから桂馬を使った手筋を紹介します。まずは両取りの手筋「ふんどしの桂」です。飛車と角を同時に狙う分かりやすく強力な手筋で、慣れたら相手が桂馬を持ち駒にしたときに自分に両取りの隙がないか探す習慣もつけましょう。
explain.en: From here we look at tesuji using the knight. First is the fork tesuji "fundoshi no kei" (the loincloth knight). It is easy to see and powerful, forking rook and bishop. Once used to it, also get into the habit of checking whether the opponent can fork you when they hold a knight.

title.ja: 図3-1 歩頭の桂

explain.ja: 次に図3-1の局面を考えます。ここから3手で相手玉を詰ますことができます。
explain.en: Next, consider Figure 3-1. From here the opponent's king can be mated in three moves.

title.ja: 図3-2 歩の頭に桂を打つ
title.en: Figure 3-2: Drop a knight on top of the pawn

explain.ja: 図3-1の局面からは3手で相手玉を詰ませることができます。1手目は歩の頭に桂を打つ▲2四桂です。
explain.en: From the position in Figure 3-1, the enemy king can be checkmated in three moves. The first move is ▲2四桂, dropping the knight on top of a pawn.

title.ja: 図3-3 空いたスペースに金を打って詰み
title.en: Figure 3-3: Drop a gold in the open space for checkmate

explain.ja: 相手にわざと桂馬を取らせ、空いたスペースに金を打てば詰みです。図3-2から桂馬を取らず△2二玉と指されても、▲3二角成で詰みとなります。これが「歩頭の桂」で、相手の歩で桂馬を取らせて駒を打つスペースを作る手筋であり、終盤の寄せでよく出てきます。
explain.en: Deliberately let the opponent capture the knight, then drop a gold into the vacated space for checkmate. Even if White does not take the knight in Figure 3-2 and plays △2二玉, ▲3二角成 is checkmate. This is the "knight on the pawn's head" tesuji: you make the opponent's pawn capture the knight to create room for a drop, and it appears often in endgame attacks.

title.ja: 図4-1 つるし桂の基本図
title.en: Figure 4-1: Basic diagram of the hanging knight

explain.ja: 図4-1の局面です。ここから持ち駒の桂馬で詰ませましょう。
explain.en: This is Figure 4-1. Mate with the knight in hand.

title.ja: 図4-2 つるし桂で詰み
title.en: Figure 4-2: Checkmate with the hanging knight

explain.ja: ▲6三桂と打てば詰みです。このように桂馬を打って詰ませる手筋を「つるし桂」と言います。桂馬は相手玉から離れた場所から王手できるので玉に直接取られず、その特長を活かした詰み筋です。
explain.en: Dropping ▲6三桂 is checkmate. This mate by a knight drop is called "tsurushi-kei" (hanging knight). The knight can give check from a distance, so the king cannot capture it directly, and this tesuji exploits that feature.

title.ja: 図5-1 美濃囲いを寄せるところ

explain.ja: 図5-1の局面は、美濃囲いを寄せようとしているところです。ここで良い手を考えます。
explain.en: Figure 5-1 shows an attempt to break a Mino castle. Consider what the good move is here.

title.ja: 図5-2 控えの桂

explain.ja: ここでは▲7六桂と打つのが好手で、次に▲7四桂と跳ねることを狙っています。このように次に跳ねる手を狙って桂馬を打つ手を「控えの桂」と言います。
explain.en: The good move here is dropping ▲7六桂, aiming to jump next to ▲7四桂. Dropping a knight to prepare its next jump like this is called "hikae no kei" (reserve knight).

title.ja: 図5-3 控えの桂からの攻め
title.en: Figure 5-3: Attack from the reserve knight

explain.ja: ▲7四桂のあと相手玉が△9二玉と逃げたら、▲6一飛成が好手です。△同銀と飛車を取られても、次の▲8二金で詰みです。控えの桂は狙いが相手にも見えていますが、受けるのは意外と難しい攻めです。
explain.en: After ▲7四桂, if the king flees with △9二玉, ▲6一飛成 is a good move. Even if White captures the rook with △同銀, ▲8二金 is then checkmate. The aim of the reserve knight is visible to the opponent, yet it is surprisingly hard to defend against.

title.ja: 図6-1 今度はどう寄せる？
title.en: Figure 6-1: How to attack this time?

explain.ja: 最後に「継ぎ桂」の手筋を紹介します。局面は先ほどと似ていますが、今度は6六の地点にすでに桂馬が控えている点がポイントです。
explain.en: Last is the "tsugi-kei" (follow-up knight) tesuji. The position is similar to the previous one, but this time a knight is already waiting at 6六, which is the key.

title.ja: 図6-2 継ぎ桂で美濃囲いが崩壊
title.en: Figure 6-2: The linked knight collapses the Mino castle

explain.ja: この局面では、いきなり▲7四桂と打つ手が成立します。桂馬の利いている地点にさらに桂馬を足す手筋を「継ぎ桂」と言い、単純ですが強力な攻めです。
explain.en: In this position, dropping ▲7四桂 immediately works. Adding another knight to a point already covered by a knight is called "tsugi-kei": simple but powerful.
